why: The ministry's own statement of RIAD, the national high-speed administrative intranet that is the ICT infrastructure sub-national offices connect into, with its operative two-phase scope of 326 then 196 administrative sites. Primary, and the instrument itself rather than commentary on it.

Commissioning of the national cloud at the Nouakchott data centre on 29 June 2026 under World Bank WARDIP: a completed step rather than an announced intention, and the shared compute and hosting layer for administration. The president of the Nouakchott Region attended, giving it a stated sub-national tie.

The DGCT's own national performance survey of all 219 communes, and the only source found that measures communal record-keeping rather than describing an intention: budget and account archiving at 82 per cent in 2021 and council deliberations at 79 per cent. It also names SIGeL, El Mouhassil and Kachel.

The Treasury's FY2025 local-finance bulletin, the first source found stating SIGeL is deployed across all urban and rural communes over the whole budget and accounting chain, with 2025 as the year of the CT 2023 application guides and receiver training. It also states its own data are drawn from SIGeL.

A distinct and completed deployment on 12 March 2026: building permits digitised for the communes of the three Nouakchott wilayas on Khadematy, running on digitised land and cadastral records with tariffs approved by the municipal councils. A working service beats the ReCAD cadastral decree, which is still a projet de décret.

The most precise dated statement found of the standing position at the peripheral facility: DHIS2 in use but not fully deployed nationally, rural health posts sending paper to health centres for entry, and no electronic medical record in primary care. It settles that capture was not digital at the rural point of service.

A completed step with named places and dates: electronic consultation registers launched at Timbedra on 16 October 2025 and Amourj on 17 October 2025, plus digitisation of the mobile clinics' register in Hodh El Chargui and Hodh El Gharbi. The only evidence found of digital capture at rural service-delivery points rather than at district level.

The ministry's own compact with the Global Partnership for Education, naming SIRAGE as the education management information system and recording that it has stabilised centrally while deconcentration to the DREN, the IDEN and schools is still to be achieved. It settles that digital capture had not reached the rural school itself.

A completed handover on 12 June 2026 of 40 laptops in Trarza, with the regional director stating the purpose is to let moughataa inspectors and school heads update data through the Siraj platform. The most direct in-window link found between school-level equipment and data entry into the EMIS outside Nouakchott.

A distinct event and a primary ministry source: the 6 March 2026 joint meeting with the digital transformation ministry ending in an agreed action plan to embed Siraj in the daily running of establishments. It beats the 500-laptop delivery, which rests only on a secondary outlet's account of a ministry brief.

The only source found carrying a territorial count of the registry offices themselves: 153 citizen reception centres received and equipped out of 168 planned in communes and administrative centres, stated by the ANRPTS director general at the system's inauguration. The founding instrument, Loi 2011-003, is already held in this queue.

The interior ministry's own first-half 2026 report to parliament, stating as a completed step that the biometric databases have been updated and interconnected with the civil-status system. Primary, and the operative link the rural reception centres work through; the parliamentary enrolment statement is already held in this queue.

The founding of the instrument itself: the national criminal data collection and recording centre, Mauritania's WAPIS/SIPAO node, inaugurated by the DGSN on 1 October 2021 under Mauritania-EU-INTERPOL cooperation. It establishes that the system exists and is centralised, with no unit count, which is the standing position.

The only figure found that counts digitally connected police and gendarmerie units: the DGSN states on 18 December 2025 that WAPIS connection is complete at 62 secondary stations, 47 police, 11 gendarmerie and 4 customs, with the operating manual entering service at the start of the year.

A distinct event on the same day: the Interior Minister's inauguration of the National Police digital platform, taking complaints and reports online and issuing criminal record certificates electronically without attending a security centre. It moves the intake point off the station counter, which bears on units outside the capital.

The clearest evidence found of an AI model in production inside a Mauritanian public administration rather than in strategy: the ministry states the road traffic system on Khidmaty rests on an artificial intelligence model developed by the Agence Numérique de l'État that identifies number plates and documents offences automatically.

The competition executed rather than announced: candidates describe registering through Khidmaty, sitting the test on tablets, and AI used to prepare the examination with same-day correction and access to marked papers. The first completed at-scale use of AI inside an administrative process found in the window.

A distinct event with an explicit ministerial statement: on 4 June 2026 the minister announced effective integration of AI into the job-search and career-guidance processes run by the national employment agency, extending AI use beyond traffic and recruitment into a service agency's own casework.

The system itself, technically described: HydroMet AI, in production for UNDP Mauritania with the ONM, civil security and the SNDR, running a stacked LSTM with Isolation Forest and the SWAT model over nine stations and four hazard types with a stated 12 per cent precision gain. The only Mauritanian sectoral system found running AI in production.

The only in-window movement in which AI enters a Mauritanian sectoral information system: the ONM and UNDP training local actors and 20 women's cooperatives at Rosso on 14 January 2026 to use the AI-based agrometeorological early warning system for yield estimation, climate risk and early crop-disease diagnosis.

The artefact rather than the plan: the only Mauritanian AI language resource found with a stated size and public availability, about 4 430 Arabic to Hassaniya pairs and 594 Hassaniya dialogue turns over 5 024 rows. No state AI centre, national model or public compute cluster was documented by any official source.

The clearest in-window institutional step tying national AI capability to the regional programme: a 9 June 2026 working session at which the ministry and a World Bank delegation agreed to widen WARDIP to artificial intelligence and mobilise additional resources for data infrastructure and data sharing.

A second distinct artefact by a different actor: the MWiML repository of CC BY 4.0 NLP datasets for Pulaar, Soninke, Hassaniya and Wolof created on 16 May 2026, with per-file counts. It broadens national-language AI capacity beyond Hassaniya alone.

Mauritania has no AI-specific law or regulator; control rests on general digital law. This is the operative instrument reaching AI's handling of people: personal data defined to include sound and image, race, health and penal data classed as sensitive, and the APD created at Article 64. The cybercrime law is already held in this queue.

The only in-window movement in which a Mauritanian regulator addresses AI misuse directly: LEAD-AI training for HAPA and its media monitoring unit covering deepfakes, synthetic media and coordinated influence campaigns, producing a draft institutional policy for responsible AI use within HAPA.

The operator's own account of Mauritania's longest-running technology hub, and the only hub found publishing counts of what it has done: 5 startups incubated, 26 pre-incubated, 40 projects supported and 6 500 participants, from a coworking space at Tevragh-Zeina, with a 2014 to 2022 timeline.

A completed opening on 21 December 2025 of the Ouadane digital space in Adrar, equipped and aimed at citizens without internet access or a smartphone, with training on the Khedematy and Aïn platforms. The clearest in-window extension of the physical digital-access estate outside Nouakchott.

A distinct and held event: the first AI hackathon of its kind in Mauritania on 17 May 2026, 25 teams of three or more across five tracks including one on local low-resource dialects, with the digital transformation ministry as key partner and the University of Nouakchott and Banque Nationale de Mauritanie as principal sponsors.
